# Results — Study 795 (Corporate-Bond-Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**cross-sectional momentum in bonds** (Jostova, Nikolova, Philipov & Stahel 2013): rank a
bond universe on trailing 6-12 month total return, go long the recent winners and short
the recent losers. We test the ETF-panel version. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `1f2efa58efab`
(11-name total-return panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return (auto-adjusted close) for an 11-name credit + Treasury bond-ETF basket, 4,903 rows, 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Universe | credit: LQD, VCLT, VCSH, HYG, JNK, EMB, BKLN, ANGL · Treasuries: SHY, IEF, TLT |
| Ranking | trailing **6-month** total return at each month-end (headline); 12m / 12-1 / 3m as robustness |
| Portfolio | equal-weight **top third long, bottom third short** (≈ 3.7 names/leg of ≈ 10.4 ranked), dollar-neutral, rebalanced monthly |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag — form on the month-*t* close, earn month *t+1* (one `shift`); one-way turnover × cost × NAV at each rebalance; the 1-unit short leg pays an annual borrow pro-rated monthly |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (auto-adjusted close) throughout — coupons folded in, both legs on the same convention |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is credit/Treasury ETFs still
trading in 2026, chosen ex post and projected backwards. A falling ETF is *shorted*, not
deleted, so this is milder than a single-name credit sort — but the vehicle list was picked
with hindsight, so any momentum premium here is a mild upper bound. A null (which is what we
find) is not manufactured *by* the bias.

## The headline — winners-minus-losers, 6-month formation, hold 1 month

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| months held (n) | 216 |
| WML mean (annualised) | **+1.63%/yr** |
| WML vol (annualised) | 10.23%/yr |
| Sharpe (gross) | **0.16** |
| **HAC (Newey-West) *t*** | **+0.80** (plain *t* = +0.67) |
| hit rate (WML month > 0) | 51.4% (Wilson 95% [44.8%, 58.0%]) |
| max drawdown / worst month | −24.2% / −18.88% |
| avg one-way turnover | 50.5% / month |

The winners-minus-losers spread earns a small positive drift, **but nowhere near
significance**: HAC *t* = +0.80, the hit rate is a coin flip (51.4%, Wilson bracket
straddles 50%), and one bad month is −18.9%. **Rank-shuffle placebo:** the real
+1.63%/yr sits against a placebo mean of +0.02%/yr (sd 1.51) over 2,000 permutations of the
monthly momentum ranking → **p = 0.152** — a random ranking beats the momentum ranking about
one time in seven. Nothing here clears the desk bar.

## Robustness — the lookback the claim also names flips the sign

| formation | mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **6m, no skip (headline)** | **+1.63%** | 0.16 | **+0.80** | 216 |
| 12m, no skip | −1.32% | −0.14 | −0.54 | 210 |
| 12m, skip 1m (12-1) | −1.19% | −0.13 | −0.54 | 209 |
| 3m, no skip | +1.93% | 0.20 | +0.93 | 219 |

The claim explicitly names a **6-12 month** formation window. On this tape the sign is not
even stable inside that window: the 6-month sort is faintly positive (*t* = +0.80) while the
12-month and 12-1 sorts are faintly **negative** (*t* = −0.54). A robust effect does not
change sign as you slide the lookback across the exact range the claim endorses.

## Subperiods — no era carries it

| era | mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-2013 (GFC + Jostova sample era) | +2.51% | 0.17 | +0.54 | 67 |
| 2014-2026 (post-publication) | +1.23% | 0.16 | +0.60 | 149 |

Neither the in-sample-era slice nor the post-publication slice clears *t* = 1, let alone
*t* = 2. There is no window where the ETF-panel spread is real.

## The timer — net of realistic costs, short leg pays borrow

Break-even one-way cost ≈ **26.8 bps** (gross +13.6 bps/month against 50.5% monthly
turnover). At realistic bond-ETF frictions:

| one-way cost | short borrow | net mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | 50 bps/yr | +0.82% | 0.08 | +0.40 |
| 10 bps | 50 bps/yr | +0.52% | 0.05 | +0.25 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps/yr | **−0.59%** | −0.06 | −0.28 |

The gross edge was never significant; costs only push the near-zero mean toward and past
zero. There is no residual to trade.

## Is there *any* edge here — or is it just being long credit?

Buy-and-hold **HYG** (high yield) earns **+5.29%/yr, Sharpe 0.52, HAC *t* = +2.47** — a
real credit risk premium, and far more than the WML spread ever made. But the WML book is
*designed* to strip that beta out (corr(WML, HYG) = −0.10, dollar-neutral), and once you do,
nothing is left: **the cross-sectional momentum tilt adds no certifiable return on top of
simply owning credit.** The long leg (+5.6%/yr) barely out-earns the short leg (+4.0%/yr),
and the gap is not distinguishable from noise.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic total-return panel with a TUNABLE planted cross-sectional momentum (seed 314);
no network. The WML engine must score ~0 on the null and light up as the planted rank
persistence grows.

| planted mom_strength | WML mean/yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.2% | **−0.11** |
| 0.06 | +3.2% | +2.51 |
| 0.12 | +11.0% | +5.30 |
| 0.20 | +24.5% | +8.59 |

Null over **20 seeds**: mean HAC *t* = **+0.14**, **|t| > 2 in 0/20 seeds**. The detector is
unbiased and has ample power — it recovers a planted momentum cleanly, so the flat real-tape
*t* = +0.80 is a true reading of the ETF panel, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The 6-month winners-minus-losers bond-ETF spread earns +1.63%/yr at
  **HAC *t* = +0.80** — insignificant — with a coin-flip hit rate (51.4%), a rank-shuffle
  placebo **p = 0.152**, and a sign that **flips negative** at the 12-month formation the
  claim also names (*t* = −0.54). No subperiod certifies it. This bond-ETF panel shows no
  cross-sectional momentum.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Break-even ≈ 27 bps one-way; the net mean is a rounding error at
  5-10 bps (*t* ≈ 0.3-0.4) and **negative** at 20 bps. Gross Sharpe 0.16, a −24% drawdown,
  and a single −18.9% month. There is no edge to charge costs against.
- **Stable across the 6-12m the claim names? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The point estimate slides
  from faintly positive at 6m (*t* = +0.80) to faintly negative at 12m (*t* = −0.54) — the
  opposite of a robust anomaly. Consistent with Jostova et al.'s own finding that bond
  momentum lives in the *single-name high-yield* cross-section, which a coarse, IG-and-
  Treasury-heavy ETF panel cannot hold.
